title: Yajurveda — Taittiriya Samhita
altTitles: The Veda of the Black Yajus School
attributionNote: The Vedic Samhitas are anonymous and collective. This is the Taittiriya recension of the Black (Krishna) Yajurveda, not the White (Shukla) Vajasaneyi Samhita; the two recensions are kept distinct.
description: The Taittiriya Samhita, the principal Samhita of the Black Yajurveda, in seven kandas. It combines ritual formulas with the prose and verse of the sacrifice, including the New and Full Moon rites, the Soma sacrifice, and the building of the fire altar. Keith's 1914 translation is complete for this recension.
historicalContext: One of the two surviving branches of the Black Yajurveda, transmitted by the Taittiriya school. Keith's translation was published in two volumes at Harvard in 1914 and remains a standard public-domain English rendering.
availabilityNote: Complete. All seven kandas of Keith's 1914 translation are streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one kanda per chapter. The passage index follows the paragraph divisions of the printed edition, not the anuvaka numbers, which are not reproduced in the served text. This is the Taittiriya recension of the Black Yajurveda, not the White Yajurveda, which is a separate school and text.
